1. Purpose & Scope
This document defines the end-to-end procedures for processing vendor invoices, approving expenditures, issuing payments, and maintaining vendor records at Meridian Partners, LLC. All Accounts Payable (AP) staff, approving managers, and the Controller must follow this SOP without deviation. Any process not explicitly addressed here must be escalated per Section 13.
Scope: All non-payroll disbursements including vendor invoices, contractor payments, employee expense reimbursements, intercompany transfers, and credit memo processing. This SOP does not cover payroll, benefits administration, or capital expenditure approvals.
2. Definitions & Vocabulary
Term
Definition
Three-Way Match
Verification that the Purchase Order (PO), Goods Receipt (GR), and Vendor Invoice all agree on quantity, unit price, and total amount within defined tolerances.
PO (Purchase Order)
A formal authorization to purchase goods or services, recorded on the PO Register sheet of ap_ledger.xlsx with a unique PO number (format: PO-YYYY-NNNNN).
GR (Goods Receipt)
Confirmation that ordered goods or services have been received, entered by the requesting department.
Non-PO Invoice
An invoice for goods or services that were procured without a purchase order. Requires retroactive approval per Section 5.3.
Invoice Variance
The difference between the invoiced amount and the PO/GR amount, expressed as a percentage: ((Invoice Amount - PO Amount) / PO Amount) * 100.
Payment Terms
The agreed-upon timeframe for payment. Common terms: Net 30 (payment due 30 days from invoice date), Net 45, 2/10 Net 30 (2% discount if paid within 10 days).
GL Code
General Ledger account code for expense classification, format: NNNN- NNN-NNNN (Entity-Department-Account). Common codes: 6 1000-100-6101000-100-100-xxx- xx Supplies), 1000-100-6300 (Travel & Entertainment), 1000-100-64006100 (Professional Services), 1000-100-6200 (Office Supplies),(Professional Services), 6200-xxx-xxxx (Of Supplies), 6300- xxx-(Software & Subscriptions), 1000-100-6500 (Facilities &1000-100-6 1000-100-6400xxxx (Travel & Entertainment), 6400-xxx-xxx (Travel & Entertainment), (Software & SMaintenance), 1500-000-9100 (Intercompany Clearing).(Software & Subscriptions), 1000-100-6500 (Facilities &ubscriptions), 6500-xxx-xxxx (Facilities & Maintenance), 1500-000- 9Maintenance), 1500-000-9100 (Intercompany Clearing).100 (Intercompany Clearing).
Batch Run
A scheduled payment processing cycle. Meridian runs payment batches every Tuesday and Thursday at 2:00 PM EST.
Department Codes
100 (Operations), 110 (Sales), 120 (HR)
Hold Status
An invoice flagged to prevent payment. Hold codes: MATCH (matching discrepancy), APPR (pending approval), DUPL (suspected duplicate), DISP-HOLD (vendor dispute), AUDIT (under review), IC-HOLD (intercompany invoice pending month-end settlement), BANK (pending bank change verification).
Vendor Master
The central record for each vendor, maintained in vendor_master.xlsx. Contains tax ID, payment terms, banking details, and 1099 classification.
2.1 Data Entry Standards
Unless a specific format is defined elsewhere in this SOP (e.g., in a template or message format), all data entered into AP records must follow these standards:
Dates: YYYY-MM-DD (e.g., 2025-09-16)
Monetary amounts: #,###.00 (e.g., 742.50 → 742.50, 1485 → 1,485.00)
Sequential IDs (Inv Reg ID, Payment ID, Match ID, Exception ID): increment the highest existing ID in that field by 1
Allowed field values:
Match Log — Result: Pass or Flag
Invoice Register — Category: PO, Non-PO, Recurring, Intercompany, Credit Memo, Employee Expense
Name fields (Entered By, Approved By, Resolved By, etc.): first initial and last name — e.g., J. Smith
Notes fields: Leave blank unless the SOP explicitly requires a note; when required, use the exact format specified in the relevant section

4. Invoice Intake & Initial Classification
All invoices arrive through one of three channels: email (ap.team@meridianpartners.com), physical mail (scanned by Office Admin), or the vendor portal.
When multiple invoices are awaiting processing, process them in chronological order by email receipt timestamp (oldest first).

4.2 Returning Incomplete Invoices
When an invoice is missing required fields, send the following email to the vendor within the same business day: To: [vendor contact email from vendormaster.xlsx; if the vendor is not yet in vendormaster.xlsx, reply to the sender’s email address]
Subject: Meridian Partners - Incomplete Invoice [INVOICE NUMBER] Body (use verbatim):
"Dear [Vendor Contact Name],
We received invoice [INVOICE NUMBER] dated [INVOICE DATE]. Unfortunately, we are unable to process this invoice because the following required information is missing: [LIST MISSING FIELDS].
Please resubmit a corrected invoice to ap.team@meridianpartners.com at your earliest convenience. We will process payment promptly upon receipt of a complete invoice.
Thank you,
Meridian Partners Accounts Payable"
Do NOT enter incomplete invoices into the Invoice Register. Do NOT place them on hold. They must be returned before entry.
4.3 Invoice Classification
After verifying completeness, classify each invoice into exactly one category. If an invoice could match more than one category, apply the following priority order: (1) Intercompany, (2) Employee Expense, (3) Credit Memo, (4) Recurring Invoice, (5) PO Invoice, (6) Non-PO Invoice. For example, a credit memo from an intercompany entity (vendor ID starting with “IC-”) is classified as Intercompany, not Credit Memo.

5. Invoice Processing & Matching
5.1 Three-Way Match (PO Invoices)
For every PO invoice, the AP clerk must verify agreement between three documents: the Purchase Order, the Goods Receipt, and the Invoice. Open the match log for the current quarter (matchlogYYYY_QN.xlsx) and record each match attempt.
5.1.1 Matching Tolerances

5.2 Duplicate Invoice Detection
After classifying an invoice (Section 4.3) but before entering it into the Invoice Register, check for duplicates using ALL THREE of the following criteria. This check applies to all invoice categories. An invoice is a duplicate if it matches on all three:
Same vendor ID, AND
Same invoice number (case-insensitive, ignore leading zeros), AND
Same invoice total amount (exact match to the penny)
If a duplicate is detected: Do NOT enter the invoice. Do NOT return it to the vendor. Place the physical/digital copy in with filename DUPL-[VendorID]-[InvoiceNumber].pdf. Post a notification to #accounts-payable with the following exact format:
DUPLICATE DETECTED: [VENDOR NAME], [VENDOR ID], Invoice [INVOICE NUMBER], Amount $[AMOUNT], Original Entry Date [DATE OF FIRST ENTRY]
Two invoices with different invoice numbers are never classified as duplicates.

Subject: AP APPROVAL REQUIRED: [VENDOR NAME] - $[AMOUNT] - Invoice [INVOICE NUMBER]

If approval is not received within the allowed timeframe: Place the invoice on APPR hold by updating its Status column in the Invoice Register. Send a courtesy email to the vendor using this template:
"Dear [Vendor Contact Name], Invoice [INVOICE NUMBER] for $[AMOUNT] is currently pending internal approval. We expect to process payment within [5/10] additional business days. We apologize for the delay. Meridian Partners Accounts Payable"
5.4 Recurring Invoice Processing
Some vendors have standing agreements for recurring services (e.g., monthly IT support, quarterly cleaning). These are listed in recurring_agreements.xlsx with the following columns: Vendor ID, Vendor Name, Service Description, Expected Amount, Tolerance (%), Frequency, GL Code, Approving Manager, Agreement Expiration Date.
For recurring invoices:
Step 1: Verify the agreement has not expired. If the Agreement Expiration Date is in the past, STOP. Do not process. Place on APPR hold and email the Approving Manager listed in the agreement to request renewal or confirmation.
Step 2: Compare the invoice amount to the Expected Amount. If the variance exceeds the Tolerance percentage, treat as an exception (Section 6.3).
Step 3: If within tolerance and not expired, approve and enter with the GL Code from the agreement. No additional approval is needed.
6. Exception Handling
Exceptions are invoices that cannot be processed through the standard matching or approval workflows. Every exception must be documented and resolved within 10 business days. Unresolved exceptions older than 10 business days are automatically escalated to the Controller.
6.1 Price Variance Exceptions
When unit price variance exceeds the tolerance defined in Section 5.1.1:
Step 1: Check if the vendor has submitted a price increase notification in the last 90 days (search email inbox for subject containing "price increase" or "rate change" from the vendor’s domain).
Step 2a – Price increase notification found: If the invoiced price matches the notified new price, update the PO on the PO Register sheet of apledger.xlsx to reflect the new pricing. Re- run the three-way match. If it now passes, approve. Update vendormaster.xlsx with the new contracted rate.
Step 2b – No price increase notification: Email the vendor requesting clarification. Use this exact subject line: "Meridian Partners - Price Discrepancy on Invoice [INVOICE NUMBER]". In the body, state the PO price, the invoiced price, and the variance percentage. Request a
corrected invoice or written justification within 5 business days.
Step 3: Post to #accounts-payable: PRICE VARIANCE: [VENDOR NAME], [VENDOR ID], Invoice [INVOICE NUMBER], PO Price $[PO PRICE], Invoice Price $[INV PRICE], Variance [X] %
6.2 Quantity Discrepancy Exceptions
When the invoiced quantity does not exactly match the Goods Receipt quantity:
If Invoice Qty > GR Qty: Place on MATCH hold. Email the requesting department to confirm whether additional items were received but not logged. 12.1 New Vendor Setup
No invoice may be processed for a vendor that does not exist in vendor_master.xlsx. To add a new vendor:

Step 3: Add a new row to vendor_master.xlsx with all required fields: Vendor ID (auto- generated, next sequential number in format V-NNNNN), Vendor Name, Tax ID, Address, Contact Name, Contact Email, Phone, Payment Terms, Bank Name, Bank Routing, Bank Account, 1099 Reportable (Yes/No), 1099 Type (NEC, MISC, or N/A), Status (Active), Created Date.

12.2 Vendor Deactivation
A vendor should be deactivated (not deleted) if there have been no transactions in the past 18 months. During month-end close, the AP Manager runs a report of inactive vendors and updates their Status to "Inactive" in vendor_master.xlsx. Inactive vendors cannot receive payments. If an invoice arrives for an inactive vendor, the AP clerk must first reactivate the vendor (change Status back to "Active" and update the reactivation date) before processing.
12.3 Vendor Statement Reconciliation
When a vendor sends a statement of account, the AP clerk must reconcile it against AP records within 5 business days. Compare each line on the vendor statement to the Invoice Register and Payment Queue sheets in ap_ledger.xlsx. Any discrepancy must be documented in an email to the vendor with subject: "Meridian Partners – Statement Reconciliation – [VENDOR NAME] – [STATEMENT DATE]".
If the reconciliation reveals that Meridian owes an additional amount not yet invoiced: Request an invoice from the vendor. Do NOT create a payment without an invoice.
If the reconciliation reveals that the vendor’s statement shows a smaller balance than Meridian’s records: Investigate for potential duplicate payments. Search the Payment Queue sheet in ap_ledger.xlsx for duplicate payment entries. If a duplicate payment is confirmed, post to #vendor-management: DUPLICATE PAYMENT FOUND: [VENDOR NAME], [VENDOR ID], Overpayment $[AMOUNT], Payment Ref [PAYMENT REF NUMBERS]. Request a refund from the vendor.

16. Audit & Compliance
All AP transactions are subject to internal and external audit. Maintain documentation sufficient to recreate any transaction from invoice receipt through payment.
16.1 Document Retention
Retain all AP records (invoices, POs, approvals, payment confirmations, vendor correspondence) for 7 years from the date of transaction. Records for the current year and prior year must be available electronically. Older records may be archived.
16.2 Audit Hold (AUDIT Status)
If Internal Audit or the Controller places an invoice on AUDIT hold, the following rules apply:
Do NOT process payment under any circumstances, even if the vendor threatens legal action.
Do NOT contact the vendor about the hold.
Do NOT modify any records related to the invoice.
Direct all inquiries about the invoice to the Controller.
Post to #vendor- management: AUDIT HOLD APPLIED: [VENDOR NAME], [VENDOR ID], Invoice [INVOICE NUMBER], Applied by [NAME]

17. Document Governance & Training
17.1 Document Review Cycle
This SOP must be reviewed at least annually by the Document Owner (Controller). The review cycle is as follows:
Scheduled Review: Effective with this revision, the Controller initiates a formal review each January. The AP Manager solicits feedback from AP staff on procedural gaps, unclear instructions, or process changes that occurred during the prior year. All proposed revisions must be documented in a draft redline and submitted to the CFO for approval before publication. The Controller may approve minor revisions (clarifications, formatting, contact updates) without CFO signoff, but must notify the CFO within 5 business days.
Ad Hoc Revisions: Revisions may be issued outside the annual cycle when triggered by regulatory changes, audit findings, or significant process failures. Ad hoc revisions follow the same approval path: drafted by the AP Manager or Controller, approved by the CFO, and recorded in the Revision History table.
Version Numbering: Major revisions (new sections, changed approval thresholds, modified tolerances) increment the whole number (e.g., 1.0 to 2.0). Minor revisions (clarifications, formatting, updated contact information) increment the decimal (e.g., 1.2 to 1.3).
17.2 Training & Acknowledgment
All AP staff, approving managers, and the Controller must read and acknowledge this SOP upon hire and after each revision. Acknowledgment is recorded by signing and dating a copy of the SOP cover page and returning it to the AP Manager for filing.
New Hire Onboarding: New AP staff must complete a walkthrough of this SOP with the AP Manager within their first five business days. The walkthrough must cover Sections 4 through 7 (core invoice processing), and Section 13 (escalation procedures).
Annual Refresher: All AP staff must complete an annual refresher during the January review cycle. The AP Manager is responsible for scheduling and tracking completion. Staff who have not completed the refresher by January 31 will be reported to the Controller.

Purpose & Scope\nThis document defines the end-to-end procedures for processing vendor invoices, approving expenditures, issuing payments, and maintaining vendor records at Meridian Partners, LLC. All Accounts Payable (AP) staff, approving managers, and the Controller must follow this SOP without deviation. Any process not explicitly addressed here must be escalated per Section 13.\nScope: All non-payroll disbursements including vendor invoices, contractor payments, employee expense reimbursements, intercompany transfers, and credit memo processing. This SOP does not cover payroll, benefits administration, or capital expenditure approvals.\n2. Definitions & Vocabulary\nTerm\nDefinition\nThree-Way Match\nVerification that the Purchase Order (PO), Goods Receipt (GR), and Vendor Invoice all agree on quantity, unit price, and total amount within defined tolerances.\nPO (Purchase Order)\nA formal authorization to purchase goods or services, recorded on the PO Register sheet of ap_ledger.xlsx with a unique PO number (format: PO-YYYY-NNNNN).\nGR (Goods Receipt)\nConfirmation that ordered goods or services have been received, entered by the requesting department.\nNon-PO Invoice\nAn invoice for goods or services that were procured without a purchase order. Requires retroactive approval per Section 5.3.\nInvoice Variance\nThe difference between the invoiced amount and the PO/GR amount, expressed as a percentage: ((Invoice Amount - PO Amount) / PO Amount) * 100.\nPayment Terms\nThe agreed-upon timeframe for payment. Common terms: Net 30 (payment due 30 days from invoice date), Net 45, 2/10 Net 30 (2% discount if paid within 10 days).\nGL Code\nGeneral Ledger account code for expense classification, format: NNNN- NNN-NNNN (Entity-Department-Account). Common codes: 6 1000-100-6101000-100-100-xxx- xx Supplies), 1000-100-6300 (Travel & Entertainment), 1000-100-64006100 (Professional Services), 1000-100-6200 (Office Supplies),(Professional Services), 6200-xxx-xxxx (Of Supplies), 6300- xxx-(Software & Subscriptions), 1000-100-6500 (Facilities &1000-100-6 1000-100-6400xxxx (Travel & Entertainment), 6400-xxx-xxx (Travel & Entertainment), (Software & SMaintenance), 1500-000-9100 (Intercompany Clearing).(Software & Subscriptions), 1000-100-6500 (Facilities &ubscriptions), 6500-xxx-xxxx (Facilities & Maintenance), 1500-000- 9Maintenance), 1500-000-9100 (Intercompany Clearing).100 (Intercompany Clearing).\nBatch Run\nA scheduled payment processing cycle. Meridian runs payment batches every Tuesday and Thursday at 2:00 PM EST.\nDepartment Codes\n100 (Operations), 110 (Sales), 120 (HR)\nHold Status\nAn invoice flagged to prevent payment. Hold codes: MATCH (matching discrepancy), APPR (pending approval), DUPL (suspected duplicate), DISP-HOLD (vendor dispute), AUDIT (under review), IC-HOLD (intercompany invoice pending month-end settlement), BANK (pending bank change verification).\nVendor Master\nThe central record for each vendor, maintained in vendor_master.xlsx. Contains tax ID, payment terms, banking details, and 1099 classification.\n2.1 Data Entry Standards\nUnless a specific format is defined elsewhere in this SOP (e.g., in a template or message format), all data entered into AP records must follow these standards:\nDates: YYYY-MM-DD (e.g., 2025-09-16)\nMonetary amounts: #,###.00 (e.g., 742.50 → 742.50, 1485 → 1,485.00)\nSequential IDs (Inv Reg ID, Payment ID, Match ID, Exception ID): increment the highest existing ID in that field by 1\nAllowed field values:\nMatch Log — Result: Pass or Flag\nInvoice Register — Category: PO, Non-PO, Recurring, Intercompany, Credit Memo, Employee Expense\nName fields (Entered By, Approved By, Resolved By, etc.): first initial and last name — e.g., J. Smith\nNotes fields: Leave blank unless the SOP explicitly requires a note; when required, use the exact format specified in the relevant section\n3. Tools, Systems & File Locations\nAll AP staff must use the following systems and file paths. Do not create ad hoc spreadsheets or store files outside the designated locations.\n3.1 Systems\nSystem\nPurpose\nAccess\nAP Ledger Workbook (ap_ledger.xlsx)\nCentral AP workbook with sheets: Invoice Register, PO Register, Payment Queue, GL Postings\nap_ledger.xlsx\nEmail\nVendor communications, approval requests, payment confirmations\nap.team@meridianpartners.com (shared inbox)\nSlack\nInternal escalations, urgent notifications, team coordination\nSee Section 3.3 for channel list\nCalendar\nPayment batch scheduling, month- end close deadlines, vendor meetings\nShared AP calendar: ap- calendar@meridianpartners.com\n\nInvoice images, supporting documentation, reconciliation files\n(see Section 3.2)\n3.2 Slack Channels\nUse the following Slack channels for all AP communications. Do not use direct messages for issues that require an audit trail.\nChannel\nPurpose\nWho Posts\n#accounts- payable\nInvoice matching exceptions, price variances, payment batch confirmations,\nAP Staff, AP Manager\n#accounts- payable\npayment failures\n\n#approvals\nApproval requests for non-PO invoices and over-threshold items\nAP Staff\n#vendor-management\nEscalations to Controller, fraud suspicion, vendo disputes > $5,000, legal threats, vendor bank changes\nAP Staff, AP Manager\n#finance\nMonth-end close status, accrual postings, reconciliation completion\nAll Finance Staff\n4. Invoice Intake & Initial Classification\nAll invoices arrive through one of three channels: email (ap.team@meridianpartners.com), physical mail (scanned by Office Admin), or the vendor portal.\nWhen multiple invoices are awaiting processing, process them in chronological order by email receipt timestamp (oldest first).\n4.1 Required Invoice Fields\nBefore processing, verify the invoice contains all of the following. If any field is missing, the invoice is Incomplete and must be returned to the vendor.\nRequired Field\nExample\nIf Missing\nVendor name and address\nApex Office Supply, 100 Commerce D Atlanta GA 30301\nReturn to vendor\nInvoice number\nINV-2025-08841\nReturn to vendor\nInvoice date\n03/15/2025\nReturn to vendor\nPO number (if applicable)\nPO-2025-01234\nClassify as Non-PO; proceed to Section 5.3\nLine items with description, qty, unit price\nCopy Paper, Qty 50, $4.99/ream\nReturn to vendor\nTotal amount due\n$249.50\nReturn to vendor\nPayment terms\nNet 30\nDefault to vendor master terms; if no vendor master entry, use Net 30\n4.2 Returning Incomplete Invoices\nWhen an invoice is missing required fields, send the following email to the vendor within the same business day: To: [vendor contact email from vendormaster.xlsx; if the vendor is not yet in vendormaster.xlsx, reply to the sender’s email address]\nSubject: Meridian Partners - Incomplete Invoice [INVOICE NUMBER] Body (use verbatim):\n\"Dear [Vendor Contact Name],\nWe received invoice [INVOICE NUMBER] dated [INVOICE DATE]. Unfortunately, we are unable to process this invoice because the following required information is missing: [LIST MISSING FIELDS].\nPlease resubmit a corrected invoice to ap.team@meridianpartners.com at your earliest convenience. We will process payment promptly upon receipt of a complete invoice.\nThank you,\nMeridian Partners Accounts Payable\"\nDo NOT enter incomplete invoices into the Invoice Register. Do NOT place them on hold. They must be returned before entry.\n4.3 Invoice Classification\nAfter verifying completeness, classify each invoice into exactly one category. If an invoice could match more than one category, apply the following priority order: (1) Intercompany, (2) Employee Expense, (3) Credit Memo, (4) Recurring Invoice, (5) PO Invoice, (6) Non-PO Invoice. For example, a credit memo from an intercompany entity (vendor ID starting with “IC-”) is classified as Intercompany, not Credit Memo.\nCategory\nCriteria\nNext Step\nPO Invoice\nInvoice references a valid PO number that exists on the PO Register sheet of ap_ledger.xlsx\nSection 5.1 (Three-Way Match)\nNon-PO Invoice\nNo PO number referenced, OR the PO number does not exist on the PO Register sheet of ap_ledger.xlsx\nSection 5.3 (Retroactive Approval)\nRecurring Invoice\nInvoice matches an active recurring vendor agreement (check recurring_agreements.xlsx)\nSection 5.4 (Recurring Processing)\nCredit Memo\nDocument has a negative total or is explicitly labeled as a credit memo/credit note\nSection 8 (Credit Memo Processing)\nEmployee Expense\nReimbursement request from a Meridian employee with attached receipts\nSection 9 (Expense Reimbursement)\nIntercompany\nInvoice from a Meridian subsidiary or affiliated entity (vendor ID starts with \"IC-\")\nSection 10 (Intercompany)\n5. Invoice Processing & Matching\n5.1 Three-Way Match (PO Invoices)\nFor every PO invoice, the AP clerk must verify agreement between three documents: the Purchase Order, the Goods Receipt, and the Invoice. Open the match log for the current quarter (matchlogYYYY_QN.xlsx) and record each match attempt.\n5.1.1 Matching Tolerances\nThe following tolerances determine whether a match passes or requires exception handling:\nCheck\nTolerance\nIf Within Tolerance\nIf Outside Tolerance\nUnit Price Variance\n±5% OR ±$25 (passes if EITHER threshold is met)\nAuto-approve; no further act\nPlace on MATCH hold; proceed to Section 6.1\nQuantity Variance\nExact match required (zero tolerance)\nProceed to price check\nPlace on MATCH hold; proceed to Section 6.2\nTotal Invoice Amount\n±$50 AND ±2%\nAuto-approve; post to GL\nPlace on MATCH hold; proceed to Section 6\nTax Amount\n±$5\nAccept invoice tax amount\nFlag for AP Manager review. T AP Manager will determine the correct tax amount and update invoice before approval.\n5.2 Duplicate Invoice Detection\nAfter classifying an invoice (Section 4.3) but before entering it into the Invoice Register, check for duplicates using ALL THREE of the following criteria. This check applies to all invoice categories. An invoice is a duplicate if it matches on all three:\nSame vendor ID, AND\nSame invoice number (case-insensitive, ignore leading zeros), AND\nSame invoice total amount (exact match to the penny)\nIf a duplicate is detected: Do NOT enter the invoice. Do NOT return it to the vendor. Place the physical/digital copy in with filename DUPL-[VendorID]-[InvoiceNumber].pdf. Post a notification to #accounts-payable with the following exact format:\nDUPLICATE DETECTED: [VENDOR NAME], [VENDOR ID], Invoice [INVOICE NUMBER], Amount $[AMOUNT], Original Entry Date [DATE OF FIRST ENTRY]\nTwo invoices with different invoice numbers are never classified as duplicates.\n5.3 Non-PO Invoice Processing\nInvoices without a valid PO require retroactive audit-trail approval before payment. The approval path depends on the invoice amount:\nInvoice Amount\nRequired Approver\nApproval Method\nMax Response Time\n$0.01 – $500.00\nDepartment Manager (budget owner for the GL code)\nEmail reply\n3 business days\n$500.01 – $5,000.00\nDepartment Manager AND AP Manager (Maria Santos)\nEmail reply from both\n3 business days\n$5,000.01 – $25,000.00\nDepartment Manager AND Controller (Raj Patel)\nEmail reply from both\n5 business days\nOver $25,000.00\nDepartment Manager AND Controll AND CFO (Marcus Webb)\nEmail reply from all thr\n5 business days\nApproval Request Email Format: To: [required approver(s)]\nCC: ap.team@meridianpartners.com\nSubject: AP APPROVAL REQUIRED: [VENDOR NAME] - $[AMOUNT] - Invoice [INVOICE NUMBER]\nBody: \"A non-PO invoice requires your approval before payment can be processed. Vendor: [VENDOR NAME] ([VENDOR ID]). Invoice: [INVOICE NUMBER], dated [INVOICE DATE]. Amount: $[AMOUNT]. Description: [FIRST LINE ITEM DESCRIPTION]. GL Code: [GL CODE]. Please reply APPROVED or REJECTED with reason. If no response is received within [3 or 5] business days, the invoice will be placed on APPR hold and the vendor will be notified of the delay.\"\nIf approval is not received within the allowed timeframe: Place the invoice on APPR hold by updating its Status column in the Invoice Register. Send a courtesy email to the vendor using this template:\n\"Dear [Vendor Contact Name], Invoice [INVOICE NUMBER] for $[AMOUNT] is currently pending internal approval. We expect to process payment within [5/10] additional business days. We apologize for the delay. Meridian Partners Accounts Payable\"\n5.4 Recurring Invoice Processing\nSome vendors have standing agreements for recurring services (e.g., monthly IT support, quarterly cleaning). These are listed in recurring_agreements.xlsx with the following columns: Vendor ID, Vendor Name, Service Description, Expected Amount, Tolerance (%), Frequency, GL Code, Approving Manager, Agreement Expiration Date.\nFor recurring invoices:\nStep 1: Verify the agreement has not expired. If the Agreement Expiration Date is in the past, STOP. Do not process. Place on APPR hold and email the Approving Manager listed in the agreement to request renewal or confirmation.\nStep 2: Compare the invoice amount to the Expected Amount. If the variance exceeds the Tolerance percentage, treat as an exception (Section 6.3).\nStep 3: If within tolerance and not expired, approve and enter with the GL Code from the agreement. No additional approval is needed.\n6. Exception Handling\nExceptions are invoices that cannot be processed through the standard matching or approval workflows. Every exception must be documented and resolved within 10 business days. Unresolved exceptions older than 10 business days are automatically escalated to the Controller.\n6.1 Price Variance Exceptions\nWhen unit price variance exceeds the tolerance defined in Section 5.1.1:\nStep 1: Check if the vendor has submitted a price increase notification in the last 90 days (search email inbox for subject containing \"price increase\" or \"rate change\" from the vendor’s domain).\nStep 2a – Price increase notification found: If the invoiced price matches the notified new price, update the PO on the PO Register sheet of apledger.xlsx to reflect the new pricing. Re- run the three-way match. If it now passes, approve. Update vendormaster.xlsx with the new contracted rate.\nStep 2b – No price increase notification: Email the vendor requesting clarification. Use this exact subject line: \"Meridian Partners - Price Discrepancy on Invoice [INVOICE NUMBER]\". In the body, state the PO price, the invoiced price, and the variance percentage. Request a\ncorrected invoice or written justification within 5 business days.\nStep 3: Post to #accounts-payable: PRICE VARIANCE: [VENDOR NAME], [VENDOR ID], Invoice [INVOICE NUMBER], PO Price $[PO PRICE], Invoice Price $[INV PRICE], Variance [X] %\n6.2 Quantity Discrepancy Exceptions\nWhen the invoiced quantity does not exactly match the Goods Receipt quantity:\nIf Invoice Qty > GR Qty: Place on MATCH hold. Email the requesting department to confirm whether additional items were received but not logged. If confirmed received, have them update the GR Qty column on the PO Register sheet of ap_ledger.xlsx first, then re-match. If not received, email the vendor requesting a corrected invoice for the actual quantity delivered.\nIf Invoice Qty < GR Qty: This is a partial invoice. Process and pay the invoiced quantity. Add a note in the match log: \"Partial invoice – [X] units received, [Y] units invoiced. Remaining units: [Z].\" Do NOT hold the invoice.\n6.3 Recurring Invoice Amount Variance\nWhen a recurring invoice exceeds the tolerance specified in the recurring agreement:\nIf variance is positive (vendor charged MORE than expected): Place on MATCH hold. Await approval or rejection within 3 business days.\nIf variance is negative (vendor charged LESS than expected): Process normally. No hold required. No approval needed. Log the variance in the match log with a note.\n7. Payment Approval & Authorization\nAfter an invoice has been matched (or approved as non-PO), it enters the payment queue. Credit Memo Processing\nCredit memos reduce the amount owed to a vendor. They must be matched against the original invoice before applying.\n8.1 Matching Credit Memos\nStep 1: Identify the original invoice referenced in the credit memo. Purpose & Scope\nThis document defines the end-to-end procedures for processing vendor invoices, approving expenditures, issuing payments, and maintaining vendor records at Meridian Partners, LLC. All Accounts Payable (AP) staff, approving managers, and the Controller must follow this SOP without deviation. Definitions & Vocabulary\nTerm\nDefinition\nThree-Way Match\nVerification that the Purchase Order (PO), Goods Receipt (GR), and Vendor Invoice all agree on quantity, unit price, and total amount within defined tolerances.\nPO (Purchase Order)\nA formal authorization to purchase goods or services, recorded on the PO Register sheet of ap_ledger.xlsx with a unique PO number (format: PO-YYYY-NNNNN).\nGR (Goods Receipt)\nConfirmation that ordered goods or services have been received, entered by the requesting department.\nNon-PO Invoice\nAn invoice for goods or services that were procured without a purchase order. Requires retroactive approval per Section 5.3.\nInvoice Variance\nThe difference between the invoiced amount and the PO/GR amount, expressed as a percentage: ((Invoice Amount - PO Amount) / PO Amount) * 100.\nPayment Terms\nThe agreed-upon timeframe for payment. Common terms: Net 30 (payment due 30 days from invoice date), Net 45, 2/10 Net 30 (2% discount if paid within 10 days).\nGL Code\nGeneral Ledger account code for expense classification, format: NNNN- NNN-NNNN (Entity-Department-Account). Common codes: 6 1000-100-6101000-100-100-xxx- xx Supplies), 1000-100-6300 (Travel & Entertainment), 1000-100-64006100 (Professional Services), 1000-100-6200 (Office Supplies),(Professional Services), 6200-xxx-xxxx (Of Supplies), 6300- xxx-(Software & Subscriptions), 1000-100-6500 (Facilities &1000-100-6 1000-100-6400xxxx (Travel & Entertainment), 6400-xxx-xxx (Travel & Entertainment), (Software & SMaintenance), 1500-000-9100 (Intercompany Clearing).(Software & Subscriptions), 1000-100-6500 (Facilities &ubscriptions), 6500-xxx-xxxx (Facilities & Maintenance), 1500-000- 9Maintenance), 1500-000-9100 (Intercompany Clearing).100 (Intercompany Clearing).\nBatch Run\nA scheduled payment processing cycle. Meridian runs payment batches every Tuesday and Thursday at 2:00 PM EST.\nDepartment Codes\n100 (Operations), 110 (Sales), 120 (HR)\nHold Status\nAn invoice flagged to prevent payment. Hold codes: MATCH (matching discrepancy), APPR (pending approval), DUPL (suspected duplicate), DISP-HOLD (vendor dispute), AUDIT (under review), IC-HOLD (intercompany invoice pending month-end settlement), BANK (pending bank change verification).\nVendor Master\nThe central record for each vendor, maintained in vendor_master.xlsx. Contains tax ID, payment terms, banking details, and 1099 classification.\n2.1 Data Entry Standards\nUnless a specific format is defined elsewhere in this SOP (e.g., in a template or message format), all data entered into AP records must follow these standards:\nDates: YYYY-MM-DD (e.g., 2025-09-16)\nMonetary amounts: #,###.00 (e.g., 742.50 → 742.50, 1485 → 1,485.00)\nSequential IDs (Inv Reg ID, Payment ID, Match ID, Exception ID): increment the highest existing ID in that field by 1\nAllowed field values:\nMatch Log — Result: Pass or Flag\nInvoice Register — Category: PO, Non-PO, Recurring, Intercompany, Credit Memo, Employee Expense\nName fields (Entered By, Approved By, Resolved By, etc.): first initial and last name — e.g., J. Tools, Systems & File Locations\nAll AP staff must use the following systems and file paths. Do not use direct messages for issues that require an audit trail.\nChannel\nPurpose\nWho Posts\n#accounts- payable\nInvoice matching exceptions, price variances, payment batch confirmations,\nAP Staff, AP Manager\n#accounts- payable\npayment failures\n\n#approvals\nApproval requests for non-PO invoices and over-threshold items\nAP Staff\n#vendor-management\nEscalations to Controller, fraud suspicion, vendo disputes > $5,000, legal threats, vendor bank changes\nAP Staff, AP Manager\n#finance\nMonth-end close status, accrual postings, reconciliation completion\nAll Finance Staff\n4. Invoice Intake & Initial Classification\nAll invoices arrive through one of three channels: email (ap.team@meridianpartners.com), physical mail (scanned by Office Admin), or the vendor portal.\nWhen multiple invoices are awaiting processing, process them in chronological order by email receipt timestamp (oldest first).\n4.1 Required Invoice Fields\nBefore processing, verify the invoice contains all of the following. If any field is missing, the invoice is Incomplete and must be returned to the vendor.\nRequired Field\nExample\nIf Missing\nVendor name and address\nApex Office Supply, 100 Commerce D Atlanta GA 30301\nReturn to vendor\nInvoice number\nINV-2025-08841\nReturn to vendor\nInvoice date\n03/15/2025\nReturn to vendor\nPO number (if applicable)\nPO-2025-01234\nClassify as Non-PO; proceed to Section 5.3\nLine items with description, qty, unit price\nCopy Paper, Qty 50, $4.99/ream\nReturn to vendor\nTotal amount due\n$249.50\nReturn to vendor\nPayment terms\nNet 30\nDefault to vendor master terms; if no vendor master entry, use Net 30\n4.2 Returning Incomplete Invoices\nWhen an invoice is missing required fields, send the following email to the vendor within the same business day: To: [vendor contact email from vendormaster.xlsx; if the vendor is not yet in vendormaster.xlsx, reply to the sender’s email address]\nSubject: Meridian Partners - Incomplete Invoice [INVOICE NUMBER] Body (use verbatim):\n\"Dear [Vendor Contact Name],\nWe received invoice [INVOICE NUMBER] dated [INVOICE DATE]. Unfortunately, we are unable to process this invoice because the following required information is missing: [LIST MISSING FIELDS].\nPlease resubmit a corrected invoice to ap.team@meridianpartners.com at your earliest convenience. We will process payment promptly upon receipt of a complete invoice.\nThank you,\nMeridian Partners Accounts Payable\"\nDo NOT enter incomplete invoices into the Invoice Register. Do NOT place them on hold. They must be returned before entry.\n4.3 Invoice Classification\nAfter verifying completeness, classify each invoice into exactly one category. If an invoice could match more than one category, apply the following priority order: (1) Intercompany, (2) Employee Expense, (3) Credit Memo, (4) Recurring Invoice, (5) PO Invoice, (6) Non-PO Invoice. For example, a credit memo from an intercompany entity (vendor ID starting with “IC-”) is classified as Intercompany, not Credit Memo.\nCategory\nCriteria\nNext Step\nPO Invoice\nInvoice references a valid PO number that exists on the PO Register sheet of ap_ledger.xlsx\nSection 5.1 (Three-Way Match)\nNon-PO Invoice\nNo PO number referenced, OR the PO number does not exist on the PO Register sheet of ap_ledger.xlsx\nSection 5.3 (Retroactive Approval)\nRecurring Invoice\nInvoice matches an active recurring vendor agreement (check recurring_agreements.xlsx)\nSection 5.4 (Recurring Processing)\nCredit Memo\nDocument has a negative total or is explicitly labeled as a credit memo/credit note\nSection 8 (Credit Memo Processing)\nEmployee Expense\nReimbursement request from a Meridian employee with attached receipts\nSection 9 (Expense Reimbursement)\nIntercompany\nInvoice from a Meridian subsidiary or affiliated entity (vendor ID starts with \"IC-\")\nSection 10 (Intercompany)\n5. Invoice Processing & Matching\n5.1 Three-Way Match (PO Invoices)\nFor every PO invoice, the AP clerk must verify agreement between three documents: the Purchase Order, the Goods Receipt, and the Invoice. Open the match log for the current quarter (matchlogYYYY_QN.xlsx) and record each match attempt.\n5.1.1 Matching Tolerances\nThe following tolerances determine whether a match passes or requires exception handling:\nCheck\nTolerance\nIf Within Tolerance\nIf Outside Tolerance\nUnit Price Variance\n±5% OR ±$25 (passes if EITHER threshold is met)\nAuto-approve; no further act\nPlace on MATCH hold; proceed to Section 6.1\nQuantity Variance\nExact match required (zero tolerance)\nProceed to price check\nPlace on MATCH hold; proceed to Section 6.2\nTotal Invoice Amount\n±$50 AND ±2%\nAuto-approve; post to GL\nPlace on MATCH hold; proceed to Section 6\nTax Amount\n±$5\nAccept invoice tax amount\nFlag for AP Manager review. T AP Manager will determine the correct tax amount and update invoice before approval.\n5.2 Duplicate Invoice Detection\nAfter classifying an invoice (Section 4.3) but before entering it into the Invoice Register, check for duplicates using ALL THREE of the following criteria. This check applies to all invoice categories. An invoice is a duplicate if it matches on all three:\nSame vendor ID, AND\nSame invoice number (case-insensitive, ignore leading zeros), AND\nSame invoice total amount (exact match to the penny)\nIf a duplicate is detected: Do NOT enter the invoice. Do NOT return it to the vendor. Place the physical/digital copy in with filename DUPL-[VendorID]-[InvoiceNumber].pdf. Post a notification to #accounts-payable with the following exact format:\nDUPLICATE DETECTED: [VENDOR NAME], [VENDOR ID], Invoice [INVOICE NUMBER], Amount $[AMOUNT], Original Entry Date [DATE OF FIRST ENTRY]\nTwo invoices with different invoice numbers are never classified as duplicates.\n5.3 Non-PO Invoice Processing\nInvoices without a valid PO require retroactive audit-trail approval before payment. The approval path depends on the invoice amount:\nInvoice Amount\nRequired Approver\nApproval Method\nMax Response Time\n$0.01 – $500.00\nDepartment Manager (budget owner for the GL code)\nEmail reply\n3 business days\n$500.01 – $5,000.00\nDepartment Manager AND AP Manager (Maria Santos)\nEmail reply from both\n3 business days\n$5,000.01 – $25,000.00\nDepartment Manager AND Controller (Raj Patel)\nEmail reply from both\n5 business days\nOver $25,000.00\nDepartment Manager AND Controll AND CFO (Marcus Webb)\nEmail reply from all thr\n5 business days\nApproval Request Email Format: To: [required approver(s)]\nCC: ap.team@meridianpartners.com\nSubject: AP APPROVAL REQUIRED: [VENDOR NAME] - $[AMOUNT] - Invoice [INVOICE NUMBER]\nBody: \"A non-PO invoice requires your approval before payment can be processed. Vendor: [VENDOR NAME] ([VENDOR ID]). Invoice: [INVOICE NUMBER], dated [INVOICE DATE]. Amount: $[AMOUNT]. Description: [FIRST LINE ITEM DESCRIPTION]. GL Code: [GL CODE]. Please reply APPROVED or REJECTED with reason. If no response is received within [3 or 5] business days, the invoice will be placed on APPR hold and the vendor will be notified of the delay.\"\nIf approval is not received within the allowed timeframe: Place the invoice on APPR hold by updating its Status column in the Invoice Register. Send a courtesy email to the vendor using this template:\n\"Dear [Vendor Contact Name], Invoice [INVOICE NUMBER] for $[AMOUNT] is currently pending internal approval. We expect to process payment within [5/10] additional business days. We apologize for the delay. Meridian Partners Accounts Payable\"\n5.4 Recurring Invoice Processing\nSome vendors have standing agreements for recurring services (e.g., monthly IT support, quarterly cleaning). These are listed in recurring_agreements.xlsx with the following columns: Vendor ID, Vendor Name, Service Description, Expected Amount, Tolerance (%), Frequency, GL Code, Approving Manager, Agreement Expiration Date.\nFor recurring invoices:\nStep 1: Verify the agreement has not expired. If the Agreement Expiration Date is in the past, STOP. Do not process. Place on APPR hold and email the Approving Manager listed in the agreement to request renewal or confirmation.\nStep 2: Compare the invoice amount to the Expected Amount. If the variance exceeds the Tolerance percentage, treat as an exception (Section 6.3).\nStep 3: If within tolerance and not expired, approve and enter with the GL Code from the agreement. No additional approval is needed.\n6. Exception Handling\nExceptions are invoices that cannot be processed through the standard matching or approval workflows. Every exception must be documented and resolved within 10 business days. Unresolved exceptions older than 10 business days are automatically escalated to the Controller.\n6.1 Price Variance Exceptions\nWhen unit price variance exceeds the tolerance defined in Section 5.1.1:\nStep 1: Check if the vendor has submitted a price increase notification in the last 90 days (search email inbox for subject containing \"price increase\" or \"rate change\" from the vendor’s domain).\nStep 2a – Price increase notification found: If the invoiced price matches the notified new price, update the PO on the PO Register sheet of apledger.xlsx to reflect the new pricing. Re- run the three-way match. If it now passes, approve. Update vendormaster.xlsx with the new contracted rate.\nStep 2b – No price increase notification: Email the vendor requesting clarification. Use this exact subject line: \"Meridian Partners - Price Discrepancy on Invoice [INVOICE NUMBER]\". In the body, state the PO price, the invoiced price, and the variance percentage. Request a\ncorrected invoice or written justification within 5 business days.\nStep 3: Post to #accounts-payable: PRICE VARIANCE: [VENDOR NAME], [VENDOR ID], Invoice [INVOICE NUMBER], PO Price $[PO PRICE], Invoice Price $[INV PRICE], Variance [X] %\n6.2 Quantity Discrepancy Exceptions\nWhen the invoiced quantity does not exactly match the Goods Receipt quantity:\nIf Invoice Qty > GR Qty: Place on MATCH hold. Patel\nM. Webb, CFO\nJan 15, 2025\n1.1\nAdded credit memo procedures\nR. Patel\nM. Webb, CFO\nMar 03, 2025\n1.2\nUpdated escalation channels; added 1099 rules\nM. Santos\nR. Patel\nApr 22, 2025\n1. Purpose & Scope\nThis document defines the end-to-end procedures for processing vendor invoices, approving expenditures, issuing payments, and maintaining vendor records at Meridian Partners, LLC. All Accounts Payable (AP) staff, approving managers, and the Controller must follow this SOP without deviation. Any process not explicitly addressed here must be escalated per Section 13.\nScope: All non-payroll disbursements including vendor invoices, contractor payments, employee expense reimbursements, intercompany transfers, and credit memo processing. This SOP does not cover payroll, benefits administration, or capital expenditure approvals.\n2. Definitions & Vocabulary\nTerm\nDefinition\nThree-Way Match\nVerification that the Purchase Order (PO), Goods Receipt (GR), and Vendor Invoice all agree on quantity, unit price, and total amount within defined tolerances.\nPO (Purchase Order)\nA formal authorization to purchase goods or services, recorded on the PO Register sheet of ap_ledger.xlsx with a unique PO number (format: PO-YYYY-NNNNN).\nGR (Goods Receipt)\nConfirmation that ordered goods or services have been received, entered by the requesting department.\nNon-PO Invoice\nAn invoice for goods or services that were procured without a purchase order. Requires retroactive approval per Section 5.3.\nInvoice Variance\nThe difference between the invoiced amount and the PO/GR amount, expressed as a percentage: ((Invoice Amount - PO Amount) / PO Amount) * 100.\nPayment Terms\nThe agreed-upon timeframe for payment. Common terms: Net 30 (payment due 30 days from invoice date), Net 45, 2/10 Net 30 (2% discount if paid within 10 days).\nGL Code\nGeneral Ledger account code for expense classification, format: NNNN- NNN-NNNN (Entity-Department-Account). Common codes: 6 1000-100-6101000-100-100-xxx- xx Supplies), 1000-100-6300 (Travel & Entertainment), 1000-100-64006100 (Professional Services), 1000-100-6200 (Office Supplies),(Professional Services), 6200-xxx-xxxx (Of Supplies), 6300- xxx-(Software & Subscriptions), 1000-100-6500 (Facilities &1000-100-6 1000-100-6400xxxx (Travel & Entertainment), 6400-xxx-xxx (Travel & Entertainment), (Software & SMaintenance), 1500-000-9100 (Intercompany Clearing).(Software & Subscriptions), 1000-100-6500 (Facilities &ubscriptions), 6500-xxx-xxxx (Facilities & Maintenance), 1500-000- 9Maintenance), 1500-000-9100 (Intercompany Clearing).100 (Intercompany Clearing).\nBatch Run\nA scheduled payment processing cycle. Meridian runs payment batches every Tuesday and Thursday at 2:00 PM EST.\nDepartment Codes\n100 (Operations), 110 (Sales), 120 (HR)\nHold Status\nAn invoice flagged to prevent payment. Hold codes: MATCH (matching discrepancy), APPR (pending approval), DUPL (suspected duplicate), DISP-HOLD (vendor dispute), AUDIT (under review), IC-HOLD (intercompany invoice pending month-end settlement), BANK (pending bank change verification).\nVendor Master\nThe central record for each vendor, maintained in vendor_master.xlsx. Contains tax ID, payment terms, banking details, and 1099 classification.\n2.1 Data Entry Standards\nUnless a specific format is defined elsewhere in this SOP (e.g., in a template or message format), all data entered into AP records must follow these standards:\nDates: YYYY-MM-DD (e.g., 2025-09-16)\nMonetary amounts: #,###.00 (e.g., 742.50 → 742.50, 1485 → 1,485.00)\nSequential IDs (Inv Reg ID, Payment ID, Match ID, Exception ID): increment the highest existing ID in that field by 1\nAllowed field values:\nMatch Log — Result: Pass or Flag\nInvoice Register — Category: PO, Non-PO, Recurring, Intercompany, Credit Memo, Employee Expense\nName fields (Entered By, Approved By, Resolved By, etc.): first initial and last name — e.g., J. Smith\nNotes fields: Leave blank unless the SOP explicitly requires a note; when required, use the exact format specified in the relevant section\n3. Patel\nM. Webb, CFO\nJan 15, 2025\n1.1\nAdded credit memo procedures\nR. Patel\nM. Webb, CFO\nMar 03, 2025\n1.2\nUpdated escalation channels; added 1099 rules\nM. Santos\nR. Patel\nApr 22, 2025\n1. Purpose & Scope\nThis document defines the end-to-end procedures for processing vendor invoices, approving expenditures, issuing payments, and maintaining vendor records at Meridian Partners, LLC. All Accounts Payable (AP) staff, approving managers, and the Controller must follow this SOP without deviation. Any process not explicitly addressed here must be escalated per Section 13.\nScope: All non-payroll disbursements including vendor invoices, contractor payments, employee expense reimbursements, intercompany transfers, and credit memo processing. This SOP does not cover payroll, benefits administration, or capital expenditure approvals.\n2. Definitions & Vocabulary\nTerm\nDefinition\nThree-Way Match\nVerification that the Purchase Order (PO), Goods Receipt (GR), and Vendor Invoice all agree on quantity, unit price, and total amount within defined tolerances.\nPO (Purchase Order)\nA formal authorization to purchase goods or services, recorded on the PO Register sheet of ap_ledger.xlsx with a unique PO number (format: PO-YYYY-NNNNN).\nGR (Goods Receipt)\nConfirmation that ordered goods or services have been received, entered by the requesting department.\nNon-PO Invoice\nAn invoice for goods or services that were procured without a purchase order. Requires retroactive approval per Section 5.3.\nInvoice Variance\nThe difference between the invoiced amount and the PO/GR amount, expressed as a percentage: ((Invoice Amount - PO Amount) / PO Amount) * 100.\nPayment Terms\nThe agreed-upon timeframe for payment. Common terms: Net 30 (payment due 30 days from invoice date), Net 45, 2/10 Net 30 (2% discount if paid within 10 days).\nGL Code\nGeneral Ledger account code for expense classification, format: NNNN- NNN-NNNN (Entity-Department-Account). Common codes: 6 1000-100-6101000-100-100-xxx- xx Supplies), 1000-100-6300 (Travel & Entertainment), 1000-100-64006100 (Professional Services), 1000-100-6200 (Office Supplies),(Professional Services), 6200-xxx-xxxx (Of Supplies), 6300- xxx-(Software & Subscriptions), 1000-100-6500 (Facilities &1000-100-6 1000-100-6400xxxx (Travel & Entertainment), 6400-xxx-xxx (Travel & Entertainment), (Software & SMaintenance), 1500-000-9100 (Intercompany Clearing).(Software & Subscriptions), 1000-100-6500 (Facilities &ubscriptions), 6500-xxx-xxxx (Facilities & Maintenance), 1500-000- 9Maintenance), 1500-000-9100 (Intercompany Clearing).100 (Intercompany Clearing).\nBatch Run\nA scheduled payment processing cycle. Meridian runs payment batches every Tuesday and Thursday at 2:00 PM EST.\nDepartment Codes\n100 (Operations), 110 (Sales), 120 (HR)\nHold Status\nAn invoice flagged to prevent payment. Hold codes: MATCH (matching discrepancy), APPR (pending approval), DUPL (suspected duplicate), DISP-HOLD (vendor dispute), AUDIT (under review), IC-HOLD (intercompany invoice pending month-end settlement), BANK (pending bank change verification).\nVendor Master\nThe central record for each vendor, maintained in vendor_master.xlsx. Contains tax ID, payment terms, banking details, and 1099 classification.\n2.1 Data Entry Standards\nUnless a specific format is defined elsewhere in this SOP (e.g., in a template or message format), all data entered into AP records must follow these standards:\nDates: YYYY-MM-DD (e.g., 2025-09-16)\nMonetary amounts: #,###.00 (e.g., 742.50 → 742.50, 1485 → 1,485.00)\nSequential IDs (Inv Reg ID, Payment ID, Match ID, Exception ID): increment the highest existing ID in that field by 1\nAllowed field values:\nMatch Log — Result: Pass or Flag\nInvoice Register — Category: PO, Non-PO, Recurring, Intercompany, Credit Memo, Employee Expense\nName fields (Entered By, Approved By, Resolved By, etc.): first initial and last name — e.g., J. Smith\nNotes fields: Leave blank unless the SOP explicitly requires a note; when required, use the exact format specified in the relevant section\n3. Tools, Systems & File Locations\nAll AP staff must use the following systems and file paths. Do not create ad hoc spreadsheets or store files outside the designated locations.\n3.1 Systems\nSystem\nPurpose\nAccess\nAP Ledger Workbook (ap_ledger.xlsx)\nCentral AP workbook with sheets: Invoice Register, PO Register, Payment Queue, GL Postings\nap_ledger.xlsx\nEmail\nVendor communications, approval requests, payment confirmations\nap.team@meridianpartners.com (shared inbox)\nSlack\nInternal escalations, urgent notifications, team coordination\nSee Section 3.3 for channel list\nCalendar\nPayment batch scheduling, month- end close deadlines, vendor meetings\nShared AP calendar: ap- calendar@meridianpartners.com\n\nInvoice images, supporting documentation, reconciliation files\n(see Section 3.2)\n3.2 Slack Channels\nUse the following Slack channels for all AP communications. Do not use direct messages for issues that require an audit trail.\nChannel\nPurpose\nWho Posts\n#accounts- payable\nInvoice matching exceptions, price variances, payment batch confirmations,\nAP Staff, AP Manager\n#accounts- payable\npayment failures\n\n#approvals\nApproval requests for non-PO invoices and over-threshold items\nAP Staff\n#vendor-management\nEscalations to Controller, fraud suspicion, vendo disputes > $5,000, legal threats, vendor bank changes\nAP Staff, AP Manager\n#finance\nMonth-end close status, accrual postings, reconciliation completion\nAll Finance Staff\n4. Invoice Intake & Initial Classification\nAll invoices arrive through one of three channels: email (ap.team@meridianpartners.com), physical mail (scanned by Office Admin), or the vendor portal.\nWhen multiple invoices are awaiting processing, process them in chronological order by email receipt timestamp (oldest first).\n4.1 Required Invoice Fields\nBefore processing, verify the invoice contains all of the following. If any field is missing, the invoice is Incomplete and must be returned to the vendor.\nRequired Field\nExample\nIf Missing\nVendor name and address\nApex Office Supply, 100 Commerce D Atlanta GA 30301\nReturn to vendor\nInvoice number\nINV-2025-08841\nReturn to vendor\nInvoice date\n03/15/2025\nReturn to vendor\nPO number (if applicable)\nPO-2025-01234\nClassify as Non-PO; proceed to Section 5.3\nLine items with description, qty, unit price\nCopy Paper, Qty 50, $4.99/ream\nReturn to vendor\nTotal amount due\n$249.50\nReturn to vendor\nPayment terms\nNet 30\nDefault to vendor master terms; if no vendor master entry, use Net 30\n4.2 Returning Incomplete Invoices\nWhen an invoice is missing required fields, send the following email to the vendor within the same business day: To: [vendor contact email from vendormaster.xlsx; if the vendor is not yet in vendormaster.xlsx, reply to the sender’s email address]\nSubject: Meridian Partners - Incomplete Invoice [INVOICE NUMBER] Body (use verbatim):\n\"Dear [Vendor Contact Name],\nWe received invoice [INVOICE NUMBER] dated [INVOICE DATE]. Unfortunately, we are unable to process this invoice because the following required information is missing: [LIST MISSING FIELDS].\nPlease resubmit a corrected invoice to ap.team@meridianpartners.com at your earliest convenience. We will process payment promptly upon receipt of a complete invoice.\nThank you,\nMeridian Partners Accounts Payable\"\nDo NOT enter incomplete invoices into the Invoice Register. Do NOT place them on hold. They must be returned before entry.\n4.3 Invoice Classification\nAfter verifying completeness, classify each invoice into exactly one category. If an invoice could match more than one category, apply the following priority order: (1) Intercompany, (2) Employee Expense, (3) Credit Memo, (4) Recurring Invoice, (5) PO Invoice, (6) Non-PO Invoice. For example, a credit memo from an intercompany entity (vendor ID starting with “IC-”) is classified as Intercompany, not Credit Memo.\nCategory\nCriteria\nNext Step\nPO Invoice\nInvoice references a valid PO number that exists on the PO Register sheet of ap_ledger.xlsx\nSection 5.1 (Three-Way Match)\nNon-PO Invoice\nNo PO number referenced, OR the PO number does not exist on the PO Register sheet of ap_ledger.xlsx\nSection 5.3 (Retroactive Approval)\nRecurring Invoice\nInvoice matches an active recurring vendor agreement (check recurring_agreements.xlsx)\nSection 5.4 (Recurring Processing)\nCredit Memo\nDocument has a negative total or is explicitly labeled as a credit memo/credit note\nSection 8 (Credit Memo Processing)\nEmployee Expense\nReimbursement request from a Meridian employee with attached receipts\nSection 9 (Expense Reimbursement)\nIntercompany\nInvoice from a Meridian subsidiary or affiliated entity (vendor ID starts with \"IC-\")\nSection 10 (Intercompany)\n5. Invoice Processing & Matching\n5.1 Three-Way Match (PO Invoices)\nFor every PO invoice, the AP clerk must verify agreement between three documents: the Purchase Order, the Goods Receipt, and the Invoice. Open the match log for the current quarter (matchlogYYYY_QN.xlsx) and record each match attempt.\n5.1.1 Matching Tolerances\nThe following tolerances determine whether a match passes or requires exception handling:\nCheck\nTolerance\nIf Within Tolerance\nIf Outside Tolerance\nUnit Price Variance\n±5% OR ±$25 (passes if EITHER threshold is met)\nAuto-approve; no further act\nPlace on MATCH hold; proceed to Section 6.1\nQuantity Variance\nExact match required (zero tolerance)\nProceed to price check\nPlace on MATCH hold; proceed to Section 6.2\nTotal Invoice Amount\n±$50 AND ±2%\nAuto-approve; post to GL\nPlace on MATCH hold; proceed to Section 6\nTax Amount\n±$5\nAccept invoice tax amount\nFlag for AP Manager review. T AP Manager will determine the correct tax amount and update invoice before approval.\n5.2 Duplicate Invoice Detection\nAfter classifying an invoice (Section 4.3) but before entering it into the Invoice Register, check for duplicates using ALL THREE of the following criteria. This check applies to all invoice categories. An invoice is a duplicate if it matches on all three:\nSame vendor ID, AND\nSame invoice number (case-insensitive, ignore leading zeros), AND\nSame invoice total amount (exact match to the penny)\nIf a duplicate is detected: Do NOT enter the invoice. Do NOT return it to the vendor. Place the physical/digital copy in with filename DUPL-[VendorID]-[InvoiceNumber].pdf. Post a notification to #accounts-payable with the following exact format:\nDUPLICATE DETECTED: [VENDOR NAME], [VENDOR ID], Invoice [INVOICE NUMBER], Amount $[AMOUNT], Original Entry Date [DATE OF FIRST ENTRY]\nTwo invoices with different invoice numbers are never classified as duplicates.\n5.3 Non-PO Invoice Processing\nInvoices without a valid PO require retroactive audit-trail approval before payment. The approval path depends on the invoice amount:\nInvoice Amount\nRequired Approver\nApproval Method\nMax Response Time\n$0.01 – $500.00\nDepartment Manager (budget owner for the GL code)\nEmail reply\n3 business days\n$500.01 – $5,000.00\nDepartment Manager AND AP Manager (Maria Santos)\nEmail reply from both\n3 business days\n$5,000.01 – $25,000.00\nDepartment Manager AND Controller (Raj Patel)\nEmail reply from both\n5 business days\nOver $25,000.00\nDepartment Manager AND Controll AND CFO (Marcus Webb)\nEmail reply from all thr\n5 business days\nApproval Request Email Format: To: [required approver(s)]\nCC: ap.team@meridianpartners.com\nSubject: AP APPROVAL REQUIRED: [VENDOR NAME] - $[AMOUNT] - Invoice [INVOICE NUMBER]\nBody: \"A non-PO invoice requires your approval before payment can be processed. Vendor: [VENDOR NAME] ([VENDOR ID]). Invoice: [INVOICE NUMBER], dated [INVOICE DATE]. Amount: $[AMOUNT]. Description: [FIRST LINE ITEM DESCRIPTION]. GL Code: [GL CODE]. Please reply APPROVED or REJECTED with reason. If no response is received within [3 or 5] business days, the invoice will be placed on APPR hold and the vendor will be notified of the delay.\"\nIf approval is not received within the allowed timeframe: Place the invoice on APPR hold by updating its Status column in the Invoice Register. Send a courtesy email to the vendor using this template:\n\"Dear [Vendor Contact Name], Invoice [INVOICE NUMBER] for $[AMOUNT] is currently pending internal approval. We expect to process payment within [5/10] additional business days. We apologize for the delay. Meridian Partners Accounts Payable\"\n5.4 Recurring Invoice Processing\nSome vendors have standing agreements for recurring services (e.g., monthly IT support, quarterly cleaning). These are listed in recurring_agreements.xlsx with the following columns: Vendor ID, Vendor Name, Service Description, Expected Amount, Tolerance (%), Frequency, GL Code, Approving Manager, Agreement Expiration Date.\nFor recurring invoices:\nStep 1: Verify the agreement has not expired. If the Agreement Expiration Date is in the past, STOP. Do not process. Place on APPR hold and email the Approving Manager listed in the agreement to request renewal or confirmation.\nStep 2: Compare the invoice amount to the Expected Amount. If the variance exceeds the Tolerance percentage, treat as an exception (Section 6.3).\nStep 3: If within tolerance and not expired, approve and enter with the GL Code from the agreement. No additional approval is needed.\n6. Exception Handling\nExceptions are invoices that cannot be processed through the standard matching or approval workflows. Every exception must be documented and resolved within 10 business days. Unresolved exceptions older than 10 business days are automatically escalated to the Controller.\n6.1 Price Variance Exceptions\nWhen unit price variance exceeds the tolerance defined in Section 5.1.1:\nStep 1: Check if the vendor has submitted a price increase notification in the last 90 days (search email inbox for subject containing \"price increase\" or \"rate change\" from the vendor’s domain).\nStep 2a – Price increase notification found: If the invoiced price matches the notified new price, update the PO on the PO Register sheet of apledger.xlsx to reflect the new pricing. Re- run the three-way match. If it now passes, approve. Update vendormaster.xlsx with the new contracted rate.\nStep 2b – No price increase notification: Email the vendor requesting clarification. Use this exact subject line: \"Meridian Partners - Price Discrepancy on Invoice [INVOICE NUMBER]\". In the body, state the PO price, the invoiced price, and the variance percentage. Purpose & Scope\nThis document defines the end-to-end procedures for processing vendor invoices, approving expenditures, issuing payments, and maintaining vendor records at Meridian Partners, LLC. All Accounts Payable (AP) staff, approving managers, and the Controller must follow this SOP without deviation. Definitions & Vocabulary\nTerm\nDefinition\nThree-Way Match\nVerification that the Purchase Order (PO), Goods Receipt (GR), and Vendor Invoice all agree on quantity, unit price, and total amount within defined tolerances.\nPO (Purchase Order)\nA formal authorization to purchase goods or services, recorded on the PO Register sheet of ap_ledger.xlsx with a unique PO number (format: PO-YYYY-NNNNN).\nGR (Goods Receipt)\nConfirmation that ordered goods or services have been received, entered by the requesting department.\nNon-PO Invoice\nAn invoice for goods or services that were procured without a purchase order. Requires retroactive approval per Section 5.3.\nInvoice Variance\nThe difference between the invoiced amount and the PO/GR amount, expressed as a percentage: ((Invoice Amount - PO Amount) / PO Amount) * 100.\nPayment Terms\nThe agreed-upon timeframe for payment. Common terms: Net 30 (payment due 30 days from invoice date), Net 45, 2/10 Net 30 (2% discount if paid within 10 days).\nGL Code\nGeneral Ledger account code for expense classification, format: NNNN- NNN-NNNN (Entity-Department-Account). Common codes: 6 1000-100-6101000-100-100-xxx- xx Supplies), 1000-100-6300 (Travel & Entertainment), 1000-100-64006100 (Professional Services), 1000-100-6200 (Office Supplies),(Professional Services), 6200-xxx-xxxx (Of Supplies), 6300- xxx-(Software & Subscriptions), 1000-100-6500 (Facilities &1000-100-6 1000-100-6400xxxx (Travel & Entertainment), 6400-xxx-xxx (Travel & Entertainment), (Software & SMaintenance), 1500-000-9100 (Intercompany Clearing).(Software & Subscriptions), 1000-100-6500 (Facilities &ubscriptions), 6500-xxx-xxxx (Facilities & Maintenance), 1500-000- 9Maintenance), 1500-000-9100 (Intercompany Clearing).100 (Intercompany Clearing).\nBatch Run\nA scheduled payment processing cycle. Meridian runs payment batches every Tuesday and Thursday at 2:00 PM EST.\nDepartment Codes\n100 (Operations), 110 (Sales), 120 (HR)\nHold Status\nAn invoice flagged to prevent payment. Hold codes: MATCH (matching discrepancy), APPR (pending approval), DUPL (suspected duplicate), DISP-HOLD (vendor dispute), AUDIT (under review), IC-HOLD (intercompany invoice pending month-end settlement), BANK (pending bank change verification).\nVendor Master\nThe central record for each vendor, maintained in vendor_master.xlsx. Contains tax ID, payment terms, banking details, and 1099 classification.\n2.1 Data Entry Standards\nUnless a specific format is defined elsewhere in this SOP (e.g., in a template or message format), all data entered into AP records must follow these standards:\nDates: YYYY-MM-DD (e.g., 2025-09-16)\nMonetary amounts: #,###.00 (e.g., 742.50 → 742.50, 1485 → 1,485.00)\nSequential IDs (Inv Reg ID, Payment ID, Match ID, Exception ID): increment the highest existing ID in that field by 1\nAllowed field values:\nMatch Log — Result: Pass or Flag\nInvoice Register — Category: PO, Non-PO, Recurring, Intercompany, Credit Memo, Employee Expense\nName fields (Entered By, Approved By, Resolved By, etc.): first initial and last name — e.g., J. Do not use direct messages for issues that require an audit trail.\nChannel\nPurpose\nWho Posts\n#accounts- payable\nInvoice matching exceptions, price variances, payment batch confirmations,\nAP Staff, AP Manager\n#accounts- payable\npayment failures\n\n#approvals\nApproval requests for non-PO invoices and over-threshold items\nAP Staff\n#vendor-management\nEscalations to Controller, fraud suspicion, vendo disputes > $5,000, legal threats, vendor bank changes\nAP Staff, AP Manager\n#finance\nMonth-end close status, accrual postings, reconciliation completion\nAll Finance Staff\n4. Invoice Intake & Initial Classification\nAll invoices arrive through one of three channels: email (ap.team@meridianpartners.com), physical mail (scanned by Office Admin), or the vendor portal.\nWhen multiple invoices are awaiting processing, process them in chronological order by email receipt timestamp (oldest first).\n4.1 Required Invoice Fields\nBefore processing, verify the invoice contains all of the following. If any field is missing, the invoice is Incomplete and must be returned to the vendor.\nRequired Field\nExample\nIf Missing\nVendor name and address\nApex Office Supply, 100 Commerce D Atlanta GA 30301\nReturn to vendor\nInvoice number\nINV-2025-08841\nReturn to vendor\nInvoice date\n03/15/2025\nReturn to vendor\nPO number (if applicable)\nPO-2025-01234\nClassify as Non-PO; proceed to Section 5.3\nLine items with description, qty, unit price\nCopy Paper, Qty 50, $4.99/ream\nReturn to vendor\nTotal amount due\n$249.50\nReturn to vendor\nPayment terms\nNet 30\nDefault to vendor master terms; if no vendor master entry, use Net 30\n4.2 Returning Incomplete Invoices\nWhen an invoice is missing required fields, send the following email to the vendor within the same business day: To: [vendor contact email from vendormaster.xlsx; if the vendor is not yet in vendormaster.xlsx, reply to the sender’s email address]\nSubject: Meridian Partners - Incomplete Invoice [INVOICE NUMBER] Body (use verbatim):\n\"Dear [Vendor Contact Name],\nWe received invoice [INVOICE NUMBER] dated [INVOICE DATE]. Unfortunately, we are unable to process this invoice because the following required information is missing: [LIST MISSING FIELDS].\nPlease resubmit a corrected invoice to ap.team@meridianpartners.com at your earliest convenience. We will process payment promptly upon receipt of a complete invoice.\nThank you,\nMeridian Partners Accounts Payable\"\nDo NOT enter incomplete invoices into the Invoice Register. Do NOT place them on hold. They must be returned before entry.\n4.3 Invoice Classification\nAfter verifying completeness, classify each invoice into exactly one category. If an invoice could match more than one category, apply the following priority order: (1) Intercompany, (2) Employee Expense, (3) Credit Memo, (4) Recurring Invoice, (5) PO Invoice, (6) Non-PO Invoice. For example, a credit memo from an intercompany entity (vendor ID starting with “IC-”) is classified as Intercompany, not Credit Memo.\nCategory\nCriteria\nNext Step\nPO Invoice\nInvoice references a valid PO number that exists on the PO Register sheet of ap_ledger.xlsx\nSection 5.1 (Three-Way Match)\nNon-PO Invoice\nNo PO number referenced, OR the PO number does not exist on the PO Register sheet of ap_ledger.xlsx\nSection 5.3 (Retroactive Approval)\nRecurring Invoice\nInvoice matches an active recurring vendor agreement (check recurring_agreements.xlsx)\nSection 5.4 (Recurring Processing)\nCredit Memo\nDocument has a negative total or is explicitly labeled as a credit memo/credit note\nSection 8 (Credit Memo Processing)\nEmployee Expense\nReimbursement request from a Meridian employee with attached receipts\nSection 9 (Expense Reimbursement)\nIntercompany\nInvoice from a Meridian subsidiary or affiliated entity (vendor ID starts with \"IC-\")\nSection 10 (Intercompany)\n5. Invoice Processing & Matching\n5.1 Three-Way Match (PO Invoices)\nFor every PO invoice, the AP clerk must verify agreement between three documents: the Purchase Order, the Goods Receipt, and the Invoice. Open the match log for the current quarter (matchlogYYYY_QN.xlsx) and record each match attempt.\n5.1.1 Matching Tolerances\nThe following tolerances determine whether a match passes or requires exception handling:\nCheck\nTolerance\nIf Within Tolerance\nIf Outside Tolerance\nUnit Price Variance\n±5% OR ±$25 (passes if EITHER threshold is met)\nAuto-approve; no further act\nPlace on MATCH hold; proceed to Section 6.1\nQuantity Variance\nExact match required (zero tolerance)\nProceed to price check\nPlace on MATCH hold; proceed to Section 6.2\nTotal Invoice Amount\n±$50 AND ±2%\nAuto-approve; post to GL\nPlace on MATCH hold; proceed to Section 6\nTax Amount\n±$5\nAccept invoice tax amount\nFlag for AP Manager review. T AP Manager will determine the correct tax amount and update invoice before approval.\n5.2 Duplicate Invoice Detection\nAfter classifying an invoice (Section 4.3) but before entering it into the Invoice Register, check for duplicates using ALL THREE of the following criteria. This check applies to all invoice categories. An invoice is a duplicate if it matches on all three:\nSame vendor ID, AND\nSame invoice number (case-insensitive, ignore leading zeros), AND\nSame invoice total amount (exact match to the penny)\nIf a duplicate is detected: Do NOT enter the invoice. Do NOT return it to the vendor. Place the physical/digital copy in with filename DUPL-[VendorID]-[InvoiceNumber].pdf. Post a notification to #accounts-payable with the following exact format:\nDUPLICATE DETECTED: [VENDOR NAME], [VENDOR ID], Invoice [INVOICE NUMBER], Amount $[AMOUNT], Original Entry Date [DATE OF FIRST ENTRY]\nTwo invoices with different invoice numbers are never classified as duplicates.\n5.3 Non-PO Invoice Processing\nInvoices without a valid PO require retroactive audit-trail approval before payment. The approval path depends on the invoice amount:\nInvoice Amount\nRequired Approver\nApproval Method\nMax Response Time\n$0.01 – $500.00\nDepartment Manager (budget owner for the GL code)\nEmail reply\n3 business days\n$500.01 – $5,000.00\nDepartment Manager AND AP Manager (Maria Santos)\nEmail reply from both\n3 business days\n$5,000.01 – $25,000.00\nDepartment Manager AND Controller (Raj Patel)\nEmail reply from both\n5 business days\nOver $25,000.00\nDepartment Manager AND Controll AND CFO (Marcus Webb)\nEmail reply from all thr\n5 business days\nApproval Request Email Format: To: [required approver(s)]\nCC: ap.team@meridianpartners.com\nSubject: AP APPROVAL REQUIRED: [VENDOR NAME] - $[AMOUNT] - Invoice [INVOICE NUMBER]\nBody: \"A non-PO invoice requires your approval before payment can be processed. Please reply APPROVED or REJECTED with reason. If no response is received within [3 or 5] business days, the invoice will be placed on APPR hold and the vendor will be notified of the delay.\"\nIf approval is not received within the allowed timeframe: Place the invoice on APPR hold by updating its Status column in the Invoice Register. Send a courtesy email to the vendor using this template:\n\"Dear [Vendor Contact Name], Invoice [INVOICE NUMBER] for $[AMOUNT] is currently pending internal approval. We expect to process payment within [5/10] additional business days. We apologize for the delay. Meridian Partners Accounts Payable\"\n5.4 Recurring Invoice Processing\nSome vendors have standing agreements for recurring services (e.g., monthly IT support, quarterly cleaning). These are listed in recurring_agreements.xlsx with the following columns: Vendor ID, Vendor Name, Service Description, Expected Amount, Tolerance (%), Frequency, GL Code, Approving Manager, Agreement Expiration Date.\nFor recurring invoices:\nStep 1: Verify the agreement has not expired. If the Agreement Expiration Date is in the past, STOP. Do not process. Place on APPR hold and email the Approving Manager listed in the agreement to request renewal or confirmation.\nStep 2: Compare the invoice amount to the Expected Amount. If the variance exceeds the Tolerance percentage, treat as an exception (Section 6.3).\nStep 3: If within tolerance and not expired, approve and enter with the GL Code from the agreement. No additional approval is needed.\n6. Exception Handling\nExceptions are invoices that cannot be processed through the standard matching or approval workflows. Every exception must be documented and resolved within 10 business days. Unresolved exceptions older than 10 business days are automatically escalated to the Controller.\n6.1 Price Variance Exceptions\nWhen unit price variance exceeds the tolerance defined in Section 5.1.1:\nStep 1: Check if the vendor has submitted a price increase notification in the last 90 days (search email inbox for subject containing \"price increase\" or \"rate change\" from the vendor’s domain).\nStep 2a – Price increase notification found: If the invoiced price matches the notified new price, update the PO on the PO Register sheet of apledger.xlsx to reflect the new pricing. Re- run the three-way match. If it now passes, approve. Update vendormaster.xlsx with the new contracted rate.\nStep 2b – No price increase notification: Email the vendor requesting clarification. Use this exact subject line: \"Meridian Partners - Price Discrepancy on Invoice [INVOICE NUMBER]\". In the body, state the PO price, the invoiced price, and the variance percentage. Request a\ncorrected invoice or written justification within 5 business days.\nStep 3: Post to #accounts-payable: PRICE VARIANCE: [VENDOR NAME], [VENDOR ID], Invoice [INVOICE NUMBER], PO Price $[PO PRICE], Invoice Price $[INV PRICE], Variance [X] %\n6.2 Quantity Discrepancy Exceptions\nWhen the invoiced quantity does not exactly match the Goods Receipt quantity:\nIf Invoice Qty > GR Qty: Place on MATCH hold. Purpose & Scope\nThis document defines the end-to-end procedures for processing vendor invoices, approving expenditures, issuing payments, and maintaining vendor records at Meridian Partners, LLC. Definitions & Vocabulary\nTerm\nDefinition\nThree-Way Match\nVerification that the Purchase Order (PO), Goods Receipt (GR), and Vendor Invoice all agree on quantity, unit price, and total amount within defined tolerances.\nPO (Purchase Order)\nA formal authorization to purchase goods or services, recorded on the PO Register sheet of ap_ledger.xlsx with a unique PO number (format: PO-YYYY-NNNNN).\nGR (Goods Receipt)\nConfirmation that ordered goods or services have been received, entered by the requesting department.\nNon-PO Invoice\nAn invoice for goods or services that were procured without a purchase order. Requires retroactive approval per Section 5.3.\nInvoice Variance\nThe difference between the invoiced amount and the PO/GR amount, expressed as a percentage: ((Invoice Amount - PO Amount) / PO Amount) * 100.\nPayment Terms\nThe agreed-upon timeframe for payment.
